messages:
sara: heads-up — after the kernel-picker change last night we're seeing a throughput dip on seq<=64 workloads when KV cache hits are frequent. p50 is fine, but p95 jumps ~2.2x. looks like shmem tiling choice + warp specialization path are interacting poorly with KV reads. anyone else observe this?

matt: saw the alerts. reproducer with llama-7b small-seq suite? i can run locally.

sara: yup. i ran a quick bench against the nightly image: tools/bench --model=llama-7b --seq=32 --batch=8 --mode=serve --pins=autotune_picker -> throughput 12.4k tok/s, p95 210ms. baseline (old-picker) was 17.1k tok/s, p95 95ms.

kevin: that's large. did you capture profiler traces? sm_efficiency / shared_load stalled?

sara: grabbed nsys & a short nvprof snapshot. key findings: shared_load_throughput spikes, l1 miss rate up ~18%, register spills increased on kernel variant A (the new pick). attaching simplified trace excerpt: ```
# kernel A (new pick) seq=32 batch=8
sm_efficiency: 62%
shared_load_throughput: 14 GB/s
l1_hit_rate: 0.72
reg_spills: 4.8k
# kernel B (old pick)
sm_efficiency: 84%
shared_load_throughput: 7 GB/s
l1_hit_rate: 0.89
reg_spills: 1.2k
```

anna: sounds like kernel A uses larger shared tile and tries warp-specialization for seq<64, which increases per-thread register pressure. KV cache path adds a handful of extra live values so spill + shmem thrash.

jon: can we confirm which kernel params the picker currently selects? iirc the picker considers (arch, seq, batch, kv_hit_ratio) but not live register count or kv-induced live ranges.

kevin: right now picker rule: if arch>=sm80 and seq<=64 -> use kernel A (tile=64, warp-specialized). else -> kernel B (tile=32). kv_hit_ratio is only used for batch routing, not for kernel variant.

priya: quick mitigation: add a cheap heuristic to pick kernel B when kv_hit_ratio>0.6 for small seq. that avoids the spill-heavy path. would be a one-line change in the picker rules.

matt: +1 for heuristic if it's low-risk. we should also add an autotune test that runs representative KV-heavy traces.

sara: i ran a quick experiment toggling tile size on kernel A from 64->32 and disabling warp specialization. numbers: throughput -> 16.5k tok/s, p95 -> 102ms, reg_spills down 70%. so definitely the tile+warp combo is culprit.

perf-bot: [ci] ran perf harness for PR #2487: model=llama-7b seq=32 batch=8 kv_ratio=0.8
- kernel A(orig): 12.4k tok/s, p95 210ms
- kernel A(tile=32): 16.5k tok/s, p95 102ms
- kernel B: 17.1k tok/s, p95 95ms

jon: good data. options: 1) change picker rule to consider kv_ratio (fast); 2) update autotuner to profile with kv access patterns (more robust but more work); 3) change kernel A implementation to lower reg usage (harder).

anna: also worth noting this only shows on sm80+ with our current register allocator. on older archs the compiler spills earlier and kernel A wasn't chosen. so the change in picker combined with compiler updates exposed this.

priya: proposal: short-term add kv_ratio branch in picker + patch tests. medium-term expand autotuner search space to include "kv_live" dimension (on/off) and add a small micro-benchmark that runs prefix-KV lookups to measure live range pressure. long-term revisit kernel codegen to avoid long-lived registers across KV loads.

matt: agree. i'll draft the picker PR with the new heuristic and add unit + perf test. can we define perf regression thresholds? prefer no >10% drop on throughput or >1.5x p95 for representative kv-heavy traces.

sara: sounds good. i'll add a failing test to the autotune CI to catch regressions: run seq={16,32,64} batch={4,8} kv_ratio={0.2,0.8} and assert throughput within threshold.

kevin: also flagging a follow-up: our profiler sampling doesn't surface live-register counts per kernel variant easily. i can add a small LLVM-metadata export in the next build to estimate live intervals for the critical ops.

jon: perfect. timeline?

matt: i'll aim for a picker PR today (canary within host-nightly in 6h). sara, can you run the kv-heavy harness on canary once it's up?

sara: yup — will validate and post numbers.

priya: please add a short note to the console release notes describing the change so support/SEs aren't surprised by minor perf diffs on non-kv workloads.

matt: ack. thanks all. tagging @perf-bot to record the ticket and baseline traces. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created perf ticket PERF-7843 and attached nsys traces from thread starter.

sara: thanks — i'll follow up with the canary numbers.

jon: quick add — consider adding an autotune config param to prefer lower-register variants under high-kv conditions. that way customer-controlled overrides are possible in Dedicated deployments.

anna: good point. ok closing loop for now.
